correctness.rationale: Every move of a four-pebble game leaves at most three stationary points. With at most two distinct stationary points, every fresh-point extension type has the same positive support throughout each dimension class. For three distinct collinear points, the additional same-line count is \(q-2\) and the off-line count is positive in dimension at least two. For a noncollinear triple, the three sides each have \(q-1\) fresh points, while the generated projective plane has exactly \((q-1)^2\) points off all sides. These are the only atomic patterns for inclusive ternary collinearity. This yields an indefinitely repeatable four-pebble strategy when the two indicated bits agree. Explicit noncollinear-three and collinear-four sentences separate all four classes. Smallest representatives contain exactly 3, 4, 7, 13 points; two- and three-variable collapses and the five-variable skew-line separator are also proved. The exact finite checker tested all 109399 ordered three-pebble assignments in ten selected spaces; the general proof does not depend on these tests.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of finite projective spaces and arbitrary finite projective planes in a geometrically canonical, single-relation signature. The classification exhibits a sharp two-bit logical invariant across all dimensions, field orders, and even non-Desarguesian plane isomorphism types; establishes exact width-2/3/4 class counts 1/2/4, optimal 13-point representatives, and a five-variable skew-line boundary showing when dimension becomes observable. These are structural, reusable limitations on finite-variable expressibility rather than isolated small-case calculations.
